title: Stop the search index from losing documents

blocks.text: The search service indexes documents by word: a `ConcurrentHashMap` from each word to the set of documents that contain it. Indexing threads add and remove documents all day, while search threads look words up and walk the sets they get back. Support tickets say that a freshly published document sometimes can't be found by a word it plainly contains, and a search now and then fails with `ConcurrentModificationException`.

items: `add(word, documentId)`: record the document under the word;
`remove(word, documentId)`: take it off again, and drop the word once no document has it.

blocks.text: When you're done, no document is lost however the indexing threads interleave, including one added at the moment the word's last other document is removed, and a search can walk a word's documents while they change. About ten lines in total.
The tests make the threads interleave the same way on every run, through the map and the sets the index is given.

cases.says: documents added under a word are found, a removed one is gone, and a word with no document left is dropped
a search that walks a word's documents finishes while another thread adds a document to that word
when the first two documents for a new word are added together, both are kept
a document added to a word while its last other document is removed is kept, and so is the word

origin.section: A Thread-Safe Map Guards Its Entries, Not the Objects Stored in Them

concepts: A concurrent map makes finding or creating an entry atomic, not later changes to the object stored in it; computeIfAbsent creates a missing value once, a shared value needs its own thread safety, and a change that must agree with the entry being there goes inside compute.
